Hi Carlos - great talking earlier. Quick recap and next steps from our call: 

- Goal: replace current rule-based search suggestion pipeline with an LLM reranker + assistant to surface product suggestions and store-level promos without increasing latency beyond 150ms p90.
- Primary constraints: per-request latency SLO (p90 <= 150ms), throughput target ~350 TPS during peak checkout flows, and strict PII handling (no customer PII left in logs).

What we agreed I would send:
1) Redwood-verified benchmark links for candidate models + latency/TPS profiles
2) prompt set we recommend (sanitized) for your evals
3) a recommended starting config (model variant, quantization, batching) and a short mutual action plan

Attachments: redwood_benchmarks_20260721.pdf (summary + latency percentiles) and acme_prompt_set_v3.jsonl (sanitized prompt pack).

High-level recommendation (short):
- Start with Llama-2-13B-instruct (q4_k_m) for best balance of quality vs latency for retrieval-augmented reranking.
- If you need lower cost and higher throughput, try RedOpt-7B-quant (our Redwood-verified variant) - 2-3x cheaper token cost and consistent p95 latency gains on A100-like infra.

Benchmarks included in the PDF:
- TPS observed (steady-state): Llama-2-13B-instruct @ 350 TPS with batching x20, p90 latency 130ms, p95 180ms (note p95 > SLO so watch tails)
- RedOpt-7B-quant: 420 TPS, p90 95ms, p95 120ms
- Latency percentiles and distribution charts per model/seq-len bucket included in Drive link below.

Next steps:
- Carlos: run the prompt pack through your eval harness (we included expected labels and eval script notes).
- Alex: can you share the short deployment config (quantization, batch settings) you tested for RedOpt?
- I will schedule a 30-min sync next week to review results and decide whether to pilot RedOpt or the 13B-instruct variant.

Thanks - happy to clarify anything.

Hey Carlos - quick answers: 

- The 13B-instruct runs in the PDF used a mixed seq-len profile sampled from live customer distributions: median request ~80 tokens, 75th ~140, 90th ~220. That tail is why p95 spikes. If your average is ~120, expect p90 around 140-160ms on the same A100 runs.

- RedOpt-7B-quant numbers were on A100-40GB with our qopt kernels and batching x25. On T4/G4dn you'll see lower absolute TPS but similar relative improvements vs baseline 13B because model size and memory locality are better for quantized 7B. For T4 we typically recommend smaller batch sizes (x8- x12) and enabling KV-prefetch in the runtime; see the deployment config in the attached PDF (page 6).

- One note on quality/regression: we included an eval slice in the prompt pack labeled "edge_promos" that historically flags quality regressions when switching to quantized variants. Please run that slice first and share false-positive rates vs your current baseline. If we see regressions, we can try mixed-ensemble: RedOpt-7B for the bulk + Llama-2-13B-instruct for the high-risk slice.

If helpful, I can spin up a short 2-hour dedicated run with RedOpt on a G4 cluster for you to sanity-check numbers - Marissa, want me to offer that to Carlos?

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
